# CREDIT. This table is taken from libfilmshell (OpenSpartan, https://github.com/OpenSpartan/libfilmshell,
# MIT licence, copyright (c) 2026 OpenSpartan; licence text in LICENSE-libfilmshell next to this file), file
# `src/game/events_data.rs`, commit ad17521 ("Generated from the game's files" in that file's own header).
# The maintainers of libfilmshell derived the event trees from the game's mode scripts; this module did not
# WHAT IS TAKEN. For each of the 11 groups of event scripts of that file, every id of its event tree (4,804
# ids, 739 responses): the script's name for the response, what kind of response it is, and for the 423 ids
# whose response gives personal score the points and the English text the game shows with them; the string
# ids of the response's own text; and whether the id is unsure (one the walk of the tree cannot place for
# certain: inside a script loop, or in Firefight's own files). The medal, announcer-line and kill-feed
# contents of the source (medal and vehicle enumerations, announcer text) are not kept: only the kind.
# WHAT IS TRANSFORMED. One tab-separated line per id. A group is named by its script files joined by "+", in
# the file's own order. The id of an event is the "rank" of this module (`lecture.EvenementDeJeu.Rang`). The
# kind is `score` when the response gives personal score, else `medal`, `announcer`, `killfeed` (checked in
# that order) or `other`. The table is regenerated from libfilmshell, not edited by hand.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated): group, rank (decimal), response name (may be empty), kind, points and English text
# (both empty unless the kind is `score`), text word ids (hexadecimal, comma-separated, may be empty), unsure
